source_title: fix: Sandbox CLI rough edges on a PDF-producing one-off: no first-party way to view the artifact, `--no-sync-output` silently ate a path argument, and scratch outputs auto-synced into the project [seen ×4]
source_content:
Problems found in this run (fix these together in one PR)

This was a pure one-off data task (CSV in, PDF report out) run entirely through `gipity sandbox run`. It completed, but three separate pieces of CLI friction sat around the produce-then-verify loop.

1. No first-party way to look at a generated PDF. The agent's whole deliverable was a PDF, and it wanted to visually confirm the layout before calling the task done. There is no platform command for that, so it hand-rolled one: a second sandbox invocation running `pdftoppm -png -r 90 docs/sales-report.pdf docs/preview` to rasterize the pages, followed by `Read` on each PNG. It then had to repeat this rasterize-and-Read cycle a second time after fixing the chart. Every sandbox-generated document artifact (PDF, docx, etc.) will hit this same wall.

2. `--no-sync-output` accepted a path argument it does not take, and the agent lost its output. On the first rasterization the agent ran `gipity sandbox run bash "pdftoppm ... && pdfinfo ..." --no-sync-output "docs/preview-*.png"` — clearly expecting the flag to be a filter ("don't sync these") or otherwise reading it as taking a value. The CLI did not reject the extra argument or warn; it ran the command, printed `Not persisted (--no-sync-output): docs/preview-1.png docs/preview-2.png`, and discarded exactly the two files the agent needed to Read. The agent had to re-issue the identical sandbox command without the flag, paying a full sandbox round-trip for nothing.

3. Sandbox output auto-sync shipped throwaway scratch artifacts into the project and to the server. Once the previews did sync, they landed in the project directory AND were pushed remote — so at the end of the run the agent spent a turn on `rm -f docs/preview-1.png docs/preview-2.png && ls -la docs/ && gipity sync`, whose output confirms the server had to be told to delete them too (`− docs/preview-2.png [delete remote]`). Intermediate verification artifacts the agent creates purely to look at its own work become part of the user's synced project unless it remembers to clean them up.

Related timing note: the sandbox calls dominated platform wall clock on this trivial job — Bash×8 accounted for 26.5s of the 31.9s in-tools time, with a max single call of 10.3s, on a 5-row CSV.

What happened in the run (verbatim):

````
1. No first-party PDF viewer — agent rasterizes its own deliverable to see it:
ASSISTANT: "PDF is built. Rendering it to an image so I can actually look at it before calling it done."
  → TOOL Bash({"command":"gipity sandbox run bash \"pdftoppm -png -r 90 docs/sales-report.pdf docs/preview && pdfinfo docs/sales-report.pdf | head -5\" ..."})
  → TOOL Read({"file_path":".../app/docs/preview-1.png"})  [OK] [{"type":"image",...}]
  → TOOL Read({"file_path":".../app/docs/preview-2.png"})  [OK] [{"type":"image",...}]
(and again after the chart fix: "gipity sandbox run --file scripts/build_report.py ... && gipity sandbox run bash \"pdftoppm -png -r 90 docs/sales-report.pd…")

2. `--no-sync-output` takes no value, but silently swallowed the path arg and discarded the needed files:
  → TOOL Bash({"command":"gipity sandbox run bash \"pdftoppm -png -r 90 docs/sales-report.pdf docs/preview && pdfinfo docs/sales-report.pdf | head -5\" --no-sync-output \"doc…"})  [OK]
     Title: Sales Report - Jan to May … Author: Gipity
     Not persisted (--no-sync-output): docs/preview-1.png docs/preview-2.png
  → TOOL Bash({"command":"gipity sandbox run bash \"pdftoppm -png -r 90 docs/sales-report.pdf docs/preview\" 2>&1 | tail -4","description":"Rasterize PDF pages and keep them …"})  [OK]
     Output files synced to this directory: docs/preview-1.png docs/preview-2.png

3. Scratch previews auto-synced into the project and had to be manually un-shipped, locally and remotely:
  → TOOL Bash({"command":"rm -f docs/preview-1.png docs/preview-2.png && ls -la docs/ && gipity sync 2>&1 | tail -3","description":"Remove preview byproducts and sync"})  [OK]
     … -rw-r--r-- 1 siverson siverson 84551 Jul 12 00:18 sales-report.pdf
     − docs/preview-2.png [delete remote]
     2 actions applied.
````

Where it shows up:
- surface: cli
- likely files (best guess, for routing): cli/src/commands/sandbox.ts, cli/src/commands/sync.ts, platform/docs/skills/sandbox-tools.md

Run context:
- user message: Here is some sales data as CSV. Analyze it and give me back a PDF report with a chart of revenue by month. month,revenue,expenses Jan,12000,8000 Feb,15000,9000 Mar,9000,7000 Apr,18000,11000 May,21000,12000

- app built: https://dev.gipity.ai/ecgiprunner/gr-0273-02-sandbox-csv-report/
- built against: srv 9.14.679 · skills 1.0.75 · cli 1.0.428

source_title: feat: Verifying a real-time canvas game: `page eval`'s headless browser can't run the render loop at speed, and its own warning points at a 'step the loop deterministically' path the platform doesn't provide [seen ×3]
source_content:
Problems found in this run (fix these together in one PR)

Problem 1 — no path to deterministic verification of a physics/animation game. The agent built a Phaser brick-breaker and tried to verify the real gameplay loop (ball bounces, bricks break, score increments, lives decrement) by driving the deployed page with `gipity page eval`. Its first two evals worked: it reached in through `import('./js/config.js')`, served the ball, and sampled ball position over time. On the third eval — the one that would have actually confirmed a brick collision and a score change — the platform returned a warning that the page painted at 14.5 fps, that waiting on real wall-clock time advances the physics far slower than it appears, that assertions after a wall-clock wait can report a false negative, and that the agent should instead 'step the app's own loop deterministically'. The platform is right, and the warning is a genuinely good diagnostic, but nothing in the CLI or the skills gives the agent a way to step a running game loop. The agent had no follow-up move: it dropped real-time verification entirely, took a static screenshot, read the PNG, and shipped the game with its core mechanic (brick collision -> score -> win/lose transitions) never exercised. This is the recurring shape for any canvas/physics/animation app on Gipity: the verify step is the only step with no working tool.

Problem 2 — `page eval` echoes the submitted script back into its own output. Every eval call printed an 'Expression: <first line of the script> (+N more lines, N chars)' header before the result. The agent already knows what it sent; the header is noise in front of the one thing it wants (the returned JSON), and on multi-line driver scripts it truncates unhelpfully.

Problem 3 — `gipity add 2d-game` was the single slowest platform call in the run (the Bash bucket's 12.7s max, of 42.5s total Bash wall clock) for a frontend-only static template with no database, no functions, and no deploy phases. In-tools time was 49.9s against 165.9s in-LLM, so nearly a quarter of the tool budget went to one scaffold call.

What happened in the run (verbatim):

````
1) The verify dead-end. Agent, after a clean deploy: "Deployed clean. Now let me verify the game actually plays by driving the live instance headlessly."

  → TOOL Bash({"command":"gipity page eval https://dev.gipity.ai/ecgiprunner/gr-0279-08-game2d-brick-breaker/ \"\nconst { game } = await import('./js/config.js');\nawait new …)  [OK]
  Eval https://dev.gipity.ai/ecgiprunner/gr-0279-08-game2d-brick-breaker/
  {"before":{"bricks":60,"state":"ready","lives":3,"score":0},"mid":{"state":"playing","vel":[311,-218],"score":0,"bricks":60},"paddleX":200}

  → TOOL Bash({"command":"gipity page eval … "})  [OK]
  {"running":true,"trace":[[348,506,0,60],[296,469,0,60],[244,433,0,60],[192,397,0,60],[146,364,0,60],[99,331,0,60]]}

(note the trace: bricks stay at 60 and score at 0 across every sample — the ball never travels far enough in real time to hit anything)

  → TOOL Bash({"command":"gipity page eval … "})  [OK]
  ⚠ Slow render: page painted at 14.5 fps. Waiting on real time (setTimeout) advances animation/physics time far slower than it looks — assertions after a wall-clock wait can report a false negative. Step the app's own loop determ…

The agent's next and final verification action is not another eval — it abandons the approach:

  → TOOL Bash({"command":"gipity page screenshot https://dev.gipity.ai/ecgiprunner/gr-0279-08-game2d-brick-breaker/ -o tmp/shot.png 2>&1 | tail -2","description":"Screenshot …})  [OK]
  Screenshot dims: 1280 × 720

Brick collision, scoring, lives, and the win/game-over screens the user explicitly asked for were never verified.

2) Script source echoed back into eval output — every call:
  Eval https://dev.gipity.ai/ecgiprunner/gr-0279-08-game2d-brick-breaker/
  Expression: const { game } = await import('./js/config.js'); (+10 more lines, 624 chars)
  {"before":{...}}

3) Scaffold wall clock (scorecard):
  tool time (platform-side wall clock, slowest first): Bash×7 42.5s (max 12.7s), Write×3 3.6s …
  → TOOL Bash({"command":"gipity add 2d-game 2>&1 | tail -40"})  [OK] Installing (server writes files + generates favicons; first add for a title can take ~10s)...
````

source_title: Scout: Tool Integration Research - WhatsApp Business API
source_content:
**Title**: WhatsApp Business API Integration for Unified Inbox

**Problem Statement**:
Our owner/operator personas—especially Maya (Home Baker) and Fatima (Food Cart Operator)—rely heavily on direct messages to capture demand, confirm orders, and coordinate pickups. Currently, WhatsApp messages are disconnected from the OHC ecosystem, requiring owners to constantly switch between their personal/business WhatsApp app and OHC. This causes missed leads, untracked deposits, and fragmented customer history, breaking the "One Assistant" promise.

**Research Report**:
*   **Market Need**: WhatsApp is the dominant messaging platform in LATAM, EMEA, and parts of APAC. Competitors like Shopify (via Inbox/plugins), Wix, and local POS systems increasingly offer WhatsApp integration.
*   **Tool Evaluated**: WhatsApp Business API (via direct Meta Cloud API or Twilio wrapper). Twilio provides a highly reliable webhook-based API that abstracts Meta's onboarding, but Meta's direct Cloud API is now much easier and cheaper for multi-tenant SaaS.
*   **Capabilities & Limits**:
    *   Supports sending/receiving text, images (great for cake/menu photos), and interactive templates (quick replies, buttons).
    *   24-hour customer service window applies: we can freely reply to inbound messages within 24h.
    *   OAuth/Embedded Signup allows a tenant (owner) to connect their own number smoothly.
*   **SaaS Viability**: Meta Cloud API charges per conversation. We can integrate this such that OHC owners bring their own Meta app setup, or OHC acts as a BSP (Business Solution Provider). For v1, allowing users to plug in a Twilio WhatsApp sender or Meta Cloud API token is viable for standalone and cloud.

**Design Doc**:
*   **Triggers**: Inbound webhook from Meta/Twilio.
*   **Action**: When a WhatsApp message arrives, the webhook handler verifies the signature and drops it into the AI Job Queue. The `Work Triage` capability categorizes it (e.g., Lead, Support, Order). The `Customer Assistant` drafts a reply based on memory/knowledge and presents it in the owner's feed.
*   **User Visibility**: Owners see WhatsApp messages natively inside the OHC feed, marked with a WhatsApp icon. They can approve AI-drafted replies or type their own. They never have to leave OHC.
*   **Integration Points**: External API webhook endpoint `POST /webhooks/whatsapp`. Needs tenant-scoped configuration for WhatsApp credentials in the `integrations` table.

**Implementation Prompt**:
Implement a WhatsApp Business API integration that connects a tenant's WhatsApp number to their OHC unified feed.
1. Add a settings section for the owner to connect their WhatsApp account (using Twilio or Meta Cloud credentials).
2. Create a secure webhook endpoint to receive inbound messages and route them to the OHC work triage pipeline.
3. Ensure the Customer Assistant can draft replies to these messages, and allow the owner to send outbound replies directly from the OHC interface.
4. Display WhatsApp messages distinctly in the work feed so the owner knows the channel origin.

**Priority**: P1
**Estimated Scope**: Large

source_title: refactor(runtime): replace boolean tool outcomes with native error semantics
source_content:
> _This was generated by AI during triage._

# refactor(runtime): replace boolean tool outcomes with native error semantics

## Current behavior

All six runtime tools share `KhalaToolResult`, a public envelope discriminated by `ok`. `khala_triage.validate` therefore reports both a conforming packet and a nonconforming packet as successful tool executions; the latter is only distinguishable through `data.valid: false`. The Pi adapter in `extensions/index.ts` serializes the complete envelope into visible tool content, so a normal validation renders as `{ ok: true, summary: "Issue conforms to the triage template.", data: { valid: true, missing: [] } }`. This duplicates success state, treats validation failure as success, and adds visual burden. The shared result contract is defined in `khala/runtime/contracts.ts`, created by runtime helpers in `khala/runtime/service.ts`, and consumed by the extension adapter, the probe renderer, policy logic, tests, and persisted session fixtures.

## Desired behavior or Goal

Use an explicit success-or-coded-error runtime result contract without an `ok` boolean. A conforming issue validation is a success; a partial, empty, or mixed-schema issue is a failure with the stable `invalid_issue_packet` error code and ordered structural violations. In Pi, collapsed tool results should look native and concise, while expanded/session/model-visible representations retain the structured action data needed for follow-up work.

## Acceptance criteria

- `KhalaToolResult` is a closed union of success `{ summary, data? }` and failure `{ summary, error }`; neither variant contains `ok`, success cannot contain `error`, failure cannot contain success `data`, and callers narrow with the error field rather than a duplicated boolean.
- `KHALA_ERROR_KINDS` includes the stable `invalid_issue_packet` code, and structured triage-validation failures preserve the validator's ordered violations, including mixed-schema conflicts rather than describing every violation as a missing section.
- `khala_triage.validate` returns success for conforming rich and accepted legacy packets, and returns `invalid_issue_packet` for partial packets, empty required sections, and mixed rich/legacy packets; malformed tool action input remains a separate `invalid_action` failure.
- The Pi integration derives native error state for Khala tool results without discarding structured errors, and extension-level coverage proves both success and failure are represented correctly under the installed Pi API.
- Collapsed Pi rendering shows one sanitized summary line with native success/error styling instead of pretty-printed result JSON; expanded rendering may show safe action-specific fields, while LLM-visible content, JSON/session output, and `details` retain the structured data required by data-bearing actions such as triage render, probe status, forge reads, and memory reads.
- Persisted or replayed result details using the previous `{ ok: ... }` shape remain renderable during the compatibility transition, especially in the existing probe renderer and session-analysis fixtures.
- Only Khala runtime-result consumers are migrated; unrelated provider, command-runner, model-route, storage, and other internal `ok` unions retain their existing contracts.

## Non-goals

- Changing triage heading rules, accepted legacy-schema behavior, the canonical issue template, action input schemas, forge operations, or CLI commands.
- Redesigning the probe tool's richer action-specific renderer or building a general TUI framework.
- Globally replacing unrelated `ok` unions outside the public Khala runtime-tool result contract.
- Removing structured action data from model-visible tool content merely to make the collapsed terminal display shorter.

## Work Plan

### Validation

- Run targeted contract, runtime-public-tool, extension, probe-renderer, policy, and session compatibility tests with `node --test --experimental-strip-types` against the affected files.
- Run `npm run test` to typecheck and execute the complete Node test suite.
- Run `npm run smoke` as the final repository gate.

### Documentation

- Update the manual runtime reference to describe the success/coded-error result contract and collapsed-versus-structured Pi presentation.
- Do not edit generated `docs/khala-runtime-tools.md` directly; update its generator only if result envelopes are intentionally added to the generated reference.
- Record the compatibility behavior for previously persisted `{ ok: ... }` result details where maintainers will find the migration constraint.

### Testing

- Add contract tests that reject `ok` in new public results and reject ambiguous success/error mixtures.
- Cover conforming rich and legacy validation, partial and empty-section validation, mixed-schema validation, stable `invalid_issue_packet` coding, exact ordered violations, and malformed-action `invalid_action` behavior.
- Add extension integration coverage for native success/error signaling, concise collapsed output, preserved structured errors, and one data-bearing action to prove follow-up data remains available.
- Retain compatibility fixtures for rendering or analyzing historical `{ ok: ... }` result details, and update policy tests that intentionally inspect Khala public result success.

## Risks

### Breaking-change

Medium risk: removing `ok` changes the public runtime-tool result envelope and all direct consumers. Treat this as an intentional breaking contract migration, keep old persisted result details readable at presentation/session boundaries, and avoid compatibility shims in newly emitted results.

### Review-size

Medium, one reviewable PR focused on `khala/runtime/contracts.ts`, Khala result helpers and call sites in `khala/runtime/service.ts`, the Pi registration/presentation adapter, affected Khala-specific policy/renderer code, targeted tests, and manual docs. Split follow-up work if implementation expands into unrelated provider result types, general TUI infrastructure, or broad generated-document redesign.

source_title: RFC: Make VoltAgent vNext an ai-sdk-first outer framework
source_content:
# RFC: Make VoltAgent vNext an ai-sdk-first outer framework

  ## Summary

  VoltAgent should become an outer framework around ai-sdk instead of a hidden abstraction layer. The primary API should
  reuse ai-sdk names, options, semantics, and types. VoltAgent-specific features must live under a `voltagent` namespace
  and provide orchestration, workflows, memory, observability, plugins, and engineering integrations.

  ## Motivation

  Current VoltAgent has already moved toward native ai-sdk models, but the core API still wraps ai-sdk calls through
  `agent.generateText(input, options)` and `agent.streamText(input, options)`. This creates semantic drift, duplicated
  types, and blocked access to newer ai-sdk capabilities.

  Source evidence:

  - `Agent.generateText(input, options)` is positional, not ai-sdk object-style.
  - `BaseGenerationOptions` is hand-written and extends `Partial<CallSettings>`.
  - `maxSteps`, `stop`, `context`, `UsageInfo`, `Tool`, and `LLMProvider` create parallel concepts.
  - `@voltagent/core` currently peers `ai:^6.0.0`, while current ai-sdk source is v7.
  - `@voltagent/core` depends directly on many provider packages.

  ## Goals

  - Align public generation APIs with ai-sdk v7.
  - Reuse ai-sdk types directly.
  - Preserve VoltAgent value: workflows, memory, guardrails, observability, server adapters, MCP/A2A.
  - Provide a low-cost escape hatch to raw ai-sdk calls.
  - Provide compat and codemod migration.

  ## Non-Goals

  - Reimplement ai-sdk retry, stream parsing, tool execution, or provider registry.
  - Add new features to legacy APIs.
  - Hide provider-specific ai-sdk capabilities.

  ## Proposed API

  ```ts
  const agent = new Agent({
    id: "assistant",
    instructions: "Helpful assistant",
    model: openai("gpt-4o-mini"),
  });

  const result = await agent.generateText({
    prompt: "Explain TypeScript",
    temperature: 0.2,
    stopWhen: isStepCount(3),
    voltagent: {
      memory: { userId: "u1", conversationId: "c1" },
      observability: { traceName: "explain-typescript" },
    },
  });
```
  Tools use ai-sdk directly:
  ```ts
  const tools = {
    get_weather: tool({
      description: "Get weather",
      inputSchema: z.object({ location: z.string() }),
      execute: async ({ location }) => ({ location, temp: 72 }),
    }),
  };
```
  Structured output uses ai-sdk Output:
  ```ts
  const result = await agent.generateText({
    prompt: "Create recipe",
    output: Output.object({ schema: recipeSchema }),
  });
```
  Escape hatch:
  ```ts
  await agent.run({ prompt: "Hello" }, async ({ ai, voltagent }) => {
    const result = await generateText({
      ...ai,
      timeout: { totalMs: 30_000 },
    });
    voltagent.attachResult(result);
    return result;
  });
```
  ## Architecture

  ### @voltagent/core

  Owns lifecycle, plugins, configuration, registries. Must not own provider wrappers or ai-sdk reimplementations.

  ### @voltagent/ai-sdk-bridge

  Thin layer for ai-sdk v7 type aliases, option composition, version checks, model resolution helpers, callback
  composition, and escape hatch context.

  ### @voltagent/workflows

  Owns workflow DSL, checkpoints, suspension, restart, workflow memory state.

  ### @voltagent/observability

  Owns OpenTelemetry, VoltOps, exporters, and ai-sdk telemetry bridge.

  ### @voltagent/compat

  Owns legacy signatures and migration shims only.

  ## Deprecations

  N+1:

  - Add new object-style API.
  - Warn on positional generateText/streamText.
  - Warn on maxSteps, stop, top-level context/userId/conversationId.
  - Warn on createTool as primary API.
  - Warn on generateObject/streamObject.

  N+2:

  - Remove legacy overloads from core.
  - Move legacy wrappers to @voltagent/compat.
  - Remove LLMProvider and provider response types from core exports.
  - Remove provider hard dependencies from core.

  ## Codemod

  Rules:

  - agent.generateText(input, opts) -> agent.generateText({ prompt/messages: input, ...opts })
  - maxSteps: n -> stopWhen: isStepCount(n)
  - stop: "x" -> stopSequences: ["x"]
  - generateObject(input, schema, opts) -> generateText({ prompt/messages: input, output:
    Output.object({ schema }), ...opts })

  - Best-effort createTool({ parameters }) -> tool({ inputSchema })

  ## Validation

  - Golden behavior tests against raw ai-sdk for text, stream, tools, structured output, callbacks, abort, retry, and
    telemetry.

  - E2E matrix for Node, Edge, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Groq, Gateway, OpenAI-compatible.
  - Bundle and install-size benchmarks.
  - Performance benchmarks for no-extension path, memory path, observability path.

  ## Risks

  - ai-sdk v7 migration can break typings.
  - ToolSet migration can break toolkit users.
  - Retry defaults changing can affect cost and reliability.
  - Stream result identity changes can break UI integrations.
  - Provider registry removal can surprise string-model users.

  ## Rollback

  - Keep @voltagent/compat.
  - Feature-flag new API in N+1.
  - Keep old default retry/step behavior in compat.
  - Pin ai-sdk v7 minor during beta/rc.

---

It is recommended to adjust the solution based on the actual situation, and it is not necessary to force compatibility with the previous major version.

source_title: fix(specs): track OpenAPI spec drift for undocumented endpoints and missing methods
source_content:
## Background During the audit performed for PR directus/directus#27316, a significant number of gaps were found between the `@directus/specs` package and the actual REST API surface of `@directus/api`. This issue is being created to better manage the process of addressing what gaps were discovered and make it easier to chunk the changes. This issue catalogs every gap found so far. It may not be exhaustive of every possible spec issue, but it covers all cases identified during a systematic review of the controller routes against the spec paths in `packages/specs/src/paths/`. I hope this catches the project up to a manageable state for future contributions. Related: directus/directus#20972, directus/directus#26539, directus/directus#25179 --- ## Currently Undocumented Paths ### Always On - [ ] **Document** `/dashboards` **and** `/panels` directus/directus#27701 Both manage Insights records (`directus_dashboards`, `directus_panels`) and follow the same shape. Bundling them in one PR is reasonable. Routes: GET, POST, GET `/{id}`, PATCH, PATCH `/{id}`, DELETE, DELETE `/{id}` for each. Source: `api/src/controllers/dashboards.ts`, `api/src/controllers/panels.ts`. - [ ] **Document** `/notifications` **and** `/translations` directus/directus#27764 Manages in-app notification records (`directus_notifications`). Routes: GET, POST, GET `/{id}`, PATCH, PATCH `/{id}`, DELETE, DELETE `/{id}`. Source: `api/src/controllers/notifications.ts`.
Manages custom translation records (`directus_translations`). Routes: GET, POST, GET `/{id}`, PATCH, PATCH `/{id}`, DELETE, DELETE `/{id}`. Source: `api/src/controllers/translations.ts`. - [ ] **Document** `/deployments` directus/directus#27767 Provider-scoped deployment management. Routes: GET `/deployments`, GET/PATCH/DELETE `/deployments/{provider}`, GET `/deployments/{provider}/projects`, GET/PATCH `/deployments/{provider}/projects/{id}`, GET `/deployments/{provider}/projects/{id}/runs`, GET `/deployments/{provider}/projects/{id}/runs/stats`, POST `/deployments/{provider}/projects/{id}/deploy`, GET `/deployments/{provider}/runs/{id}`, POST `/deployments/{provider}/runs/{id}/cancel`, GET `/deployments/{provider}/dashboard`. Source: `api/src/controllers/deployment.ts`. - [ ] **Document** `/shares` directus/directus#27763 Manages content share records (`directus_shares`). Includes three special-purpose endpoints beyond the standard CRUD set. Routes: GET, POST, GET `/{id}`, PATCH, PATCH `/{id}`, DELETE, DELETE `/{id}`, POST `/shares/auth` (no user credential required, accepts optional password), POST `/shares/invite` (send email invitations), GET `/shares/info/{id}` (public endpoint, no authentication required, validates expiry and usage limits). Source: `api/src/controllers/shares.ts`. - [ ] **Document** `/extensions/registry`, `/extensions/registry/account/{pk}`, `/extensions/registry/extension/{pk}`, `/extensions/registry/install`, `/extensions/registry/reinstall`, `/extensions/registry/uninstall/{pk}`, `/extensions/{pk}` (DELETE), and `/extensions/sources/{chunk}` Only `GET /extensions`, `PATCH /extensions/{name}`, and `PATCH /extensions/{bundle}/{name}` are currently documented (`packages/specs/src/paths/extensions/`). The registry browse/install/uninstall routes and the `DELETE /extensions/{pk}` / `GET /extensions/sources/{chunk}` routes have no spec coverage at all. Source: `api/src/controllers/extensions.ts`. ### ENV Gated - [ ] **Document ENV-gated subsystems:** `/files/tus`**,** `/mcp`**,** `/mcp-oauth/clients` directus/directus#27766 Use the same env-gating pattern introduced for `/metrics` in PR directus/directus#27316. `/files/tus` (requires `TUS_ENABLED=true`): POST `/files/tus`, HEAD `/files/tus/{id}`, OPTIONS `/files/tus/{id}`, PATCH `/files/tus/{id}`, DELETE `/files/tus/{id}`. Source: `api/src/controllers/tus.ts`. `/mcp` (requires `mcp_enabled` system setting): GET `/mcp`, POST `/mcp`. Source: `api/src/controllers/mcp/index.ts`. `/mcp-oauth/clients` (requires `MCP_OAUTH_ENABLED=true`): GET, POST, GET `/{id}`, DELETE, DELETE `/{id}`. Source: `api/src/controllers/mcp/oauth-clients.ts`. ## Paths with incorrect documentation - [ ] **Add missing methods to** `/server`**,** `/files`**, and** `/flows` directus/directus#27765 `/server`: GET `/server/health` (200 or 503, requires `HEALTHCHECK_ENABLED != false`) `/files`: POST `/files/import` (import file from remote URL, accepts `url`, optional `data` and `filterMimeType`). `/flows`: GET `/flows/trigger/{id}` and POST `/flows/trigger/{id}`. - [x] **Add missing methods to** `/users` directus/directus#27761 `/users`: POST `/users/register` (public self-registration, rate-limited, accepts `email`, `password`, optional `first_name`, `last_name`, `verification_url`), GET `/users/register/verify-email` (email verification redirect), POST `/users/me/tfa/generate` (returns secret and QR code URI), POST `/users/me/tfa/enable` (requires `secret` and `otp`). Note: `/users/me/tfa/disable` and `/users/{id}/tfa/disable` are already documented. - [ ] **Remove incorrect query parameters from** `/collections` **and** `/fields` directus/directus#27762 Confirmed by @ComfortablyCoding during review of PR directus/directus#27316 with references to the relevant controller lines. GET `/collections`: remove `Offset` and `Meta` (API accepts no query parameters on this endpoint). GET `/fields`: remove `Limit`, `Page`, and `Sort` (API accepts no query parameters on this endpoint). GET `/fields/{collection}`: remove `Sort` (API accepts no query parameters on this endpoint). - [ ] **Add SEARCH method to all affected endpoints** directus/directus#27760 The API implements the SEARCH HTTP method as an alternative to GET for complex filtered queries. It is not documented on any endpoint. Affected paths (at minimum): `/collections`, `/comments`, `/dashboards`, `/files`, `/folders`, `/items/{collection}`, `/notifications`, `/operations`, `/panels`, `/permissions`, `/presets`, `/revisions`, `/roles`, `/shares`, `/translations`, `/users`, `/versions`. ## Validation warnings When loading the generated OAS from `GET /server/specs/oas` without an authentication token, two pre-existing validation warnings appear for the `Query` and `x-metadata` schema references. They do not appear when the spec is generated with an authenticated token. These are not introduced by any of the changes in PR directus/directus#27316 and may resolve as spec coverage catches up. ## Known exclusions `/license` is intentionally not exposed in the public spec (confirmed as internal use only by @ComfortablyCoding during review of PR directus/directus#27316). `/ai/chat`, `/ai/object`, and `/ai/files` (all under the `AI_ENABLED=true` gate) are intentionally not exposed in the public spec. All three check `req.accountability?.app` and reject non-studio sessions with a 403. They are studio-internal tooling, not a public API surface. Confirmed by PR descriptions: #26259 ("intended for in-studio use only"), #26862 ("requires `app: true` accountability"), #26722 (server-side proxy for the studio file-attachment feature). Source: `api/src/ai/chat/controllers/chat.post.ts`, `api/src/ai/chat/controllers/object.post.ts`, `api/src/ai/files/controllers/upload.ts`. ## Testing note All gaps above were identified by comparing controller route registrations in `api/src/controllers/` against the path directories in `packages/specs/src/paths/`. Testing was performed against a bare database. Validation of response shapes against real data should use the [simple-website-cms template]() to populate realistic content before verifying spec accuracy end-to-end. - [ ] Test Against CMS Template - Close this issue once all above checks are done and the CMS issue is verified. ## GENERAL CLEANUP - [ ] Responses should match the appropriate StatusCode - '204': response will be a ref per https://github.com/directus/directus/pull/27857#discussion_r3539779409 > `/auth/logout` responds 204 (currently documented as 200) > `/utils/{collection}/export` responds 204 (currently documented as 200) > `/schema/diff` has a non-standard 204 - '403': response is now a ref, many paths are undocumented for 403 but it is a meaningful response. It is distinct from 401 (unauthenticated) per https://github.com/directus/directus/pull/27316#issuecomment-4918300427 - [ ] `items.yaml` schema: intentionally blank per https://github.com/directus/directus/pull/27316#issuecomment-4908405007 `items.yaml` still has an empty schema (intentional from directus/directus#16294). I'm not sure I understand it well enough to know that adding an empty object schema will allow tests to pass natively and not create any issues. https://github.com/directus/directus/blob/e86e4a60c9d7efa2b84a2b76dc43769f766b6651/packages/specs/src/paths/items/items.yaml#L38-L49 > ```diff > # I think the fix is to... > - schema: > + schema: {} > ``` I want to get around the swagger-cli validate error that "schema must be object". More research to be done on the OpenAPI Spec versions; my guess is the version is important with this fix. - [ ] ensure punctuation usage is consistent per https://github.com/directus/directus/pull/27857#issuecomment-4909775612 Currently there are inconsistencies with punctuation usage in summary/description fields. After everything is fixed we should nit the punctuation so it's all consistent. - [ ] directus/directus#27890 for writeOnly and readOnly fields - [ ] directus/directus#27900 for missing objects in `query.yaml` and `paramters/*.yaml` --- ## Deferred I'm unable to see Directus team LINEAR or project boards; it may make sense to add these somewhere or provide guidance on the following: * Configuring the build/release CICD Pipeline to generate a OASSpec to ensure that the documentation on [http://directus.com/docs/api]() always matches the current release. * Addressed ✅ via directus/directus#27856 ~~Update the PR Template to clarify that the SPECS package should be reviewed for any changes to API package; I think this is the cause of a lot of the drift.~~ * directus/directus#25179 has an open Linear Ticket related to SEO plugin that I'm not even sure how I'd begin to introduce a fix for but I'm interested in potentially exploring this as well. * Add some sort of readme.md or contributing.md to the package/specs to explain some of the lesser understood or customized elements of the specs package (i.e. ENV gating, x-metadata)
tagged per previous comments in related issues * @phazonoverload - [https://github.com/directus/directus/issues/20972#issuecomment-2231675137]() * @ANKANJAGTAP - [https://github.com/directus/directus/issues/26539#issuecomment-3817646499]()

source_title: E2E Robustness epic: 7-criterion gate (OSS + Cloud + Landing + cross-repo)
source_content:
## Purpose

Tracking issue for the E2E robustness investment (mandate 2026-05-17). A cron fires every 2 hours to close one gap per fire until all 7 criteria below are green for 7 consecutive days, at which point it posts a final summary and is disabled.

## 7 Criteria (all must be green for 7 consecutive days)

- [x] **C1 OSS golden path** -- wheel install + real OpenClaw + send message + all 9 canonical tabs render without auth errors. Runs on every PR in under 5 min. Workflow: `oss-golden-path.yml` + `tests/test_e2e_oss_golden_path.py`. **GREEN confirmed 2026-05-31: "OSS golden path (wheel + OpenClaw + 9 tabs)" PASSED on PR #2382 in 1m 12s.**
- [x] **C2 Cloud golden path** -- synthetic signup + daemon connect + sync synthetic message + cloud dashboard renders `/cloud`, `/cloud/node/<id>`, `/cloud/account`, `/cloud/team`, `/cloud/billing` without JS errors. Runs on every PR in under 8 min. Workflow: `e2e.yml` (job: `Cloud golden-path browser E2E`). **GREEN confirmed 2026-05-31: workflow runs on every PR, PASSED on cloud#1168.**
- [x] **C3 Landing golden path** -- hero loads + click Get Started + signup form submits + OTP delivered + handoff to cloud signup. Runs on every PR in under 3 min. Workflow: `landing-golden-path.yml` (job: `Landing golden path (C3)`). **GREEN confirmed 2026-05-31: PASSED on clawmetry-landing#384 in 18s.**
- [x] **C4 Cross-repo handoff** -- landing signup to cloud account creation to daemon pair to first sync event lands. End-to-end across all 3 repos in under 10 min. Workflow: `cross-repo-handoff.yml` (job: `Cross-repo handoff (C4)`). **GREEN confirmed 2026-05-31: PASSED on PR #2382 in 20s.**
- [x] **C5 Visual-diff covers ALL tabs post-auth** -- user-reported 2026-05-17: "gateway token not passed for OSS so it never displays other screens." Every OSS dashboard tab screenshots post-login. Same for cloud `/cloud/node/<id>` deep-link. Workflow: `pr-screenshots.yml` (job: `visual-diff`). **GREEN confirmed 2026-05-31: PASSED on PR #2382 in 5m 51s.**
- [ ] **C6 Required-status-checks** -- every workflow above is marked required in branch protection / ruleset across all 3 repos. PRs cannot merge unless E2E passes. **RED -- requires manual action (see below).**
- [x] **C7 Failure quarantine** -- flaky failures quarantined within 24h, not silently retried forever. Workflow: `quarantine-sweep.yml`. **GREEN: infrastructure in place, 0 tests currently quarantined (last triage 2026-05-22).**

---

## Current state (assessed 2026-05-31)

| Criterion | Status | Job name (for required-status-check) | Notes |
|-----------|--------|---------------------------------------|-------|
| C1 OSS golden path | GREEN | `OSS golden path (wheel + OpenClaw + 9 tabs)` | PASSED PR #2382 today in 1m 12s. |
| C2 Cloud golden path | GREEN | `Cloud golden-path browser E2E` | PASSED cloud#1168. `e2e.yml` runs on every PR. |
| C3 Landing golden path | GREEN | `Landing golden path (C3)` | PASSED clawmetry-landing#384 today in 18s. |
| C4 Cross-repo handoff | GREEN | `Cross-repo handoff (C4)` | PASSED PR #2382 today in 20s. |
| C5 Visual-diff all tabs | GREEN | `visual-diff` | PASSED PR #2382 today in 5m 51s. |
| C6 Required-status-checks | RED | N/A | Workflows exist but NONE are required. 1 manual step blocks the 7-day countdown (see C6 action below). |
| C7 Failure quarantine | GREEN | N/A | `quarantine.txt` + conftest hook + `quarantine-sweep.yml` all in place. 0 tests quarantined. |

**6 of 7 criteria green. C6 is the only blocker.**

---

## C6 manual action required

None of the E2E workflows are configured as required status checks. This means PRs can merge even when E2E fails. The GitHub branch protection API cannot be set via Actions YAML -- it requires a repo admin to click or run a gh CLI command.

**Option A: GitHub Settings UI**

For each repo, go to Settings -> Rules -> Rulesets (or Branches -> Branch protection rules for classic protection), select the `main` branch rule, and add each job name as a required status check:

| Repo | Job name to add |
|------|-----------------|
| vivekchand/clawmetry | `OSS golden path (wheel + OpenClaw + 9 tabs)` |
| vivekchand/clawmetry | `Cross-repo handoff (C4)` |
| vivekchand/clawmetry | `visual-diff` |
| vivekchand/clawmetry-cloud | `Cloud golden-path browser E2E` |
| vivekchand/clawmetry-landing | `Landing golden path (C3)` |

**Option B: gh CLI (run locally with admin PAT)**

```bash
# clawmetry: add three required checks
gh api repos/vivekchand/clawmetry/branches/main/protection \
  --method PUT \
  -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" \
  -F "required_status_checks[strict]=false" \
  -F "required_status_checks[contexts][]=OSS golden path (wheel + OpenClaw + 9 tabs)" \
  -F "required_status_checks[contexts][]=Cross-repo handoff (C4)" \
  -F "required_status_checks[contexts][]=visual-diff" \
  -F "enforce_admins=false" \
  -F "required_pull_request_reviews=null" \
  -F "restrictions=null"

# clawmetry-cloud: add one required check
gh api repos/vivekchand/clawmetry-cloud/branches/main/protection \
  --method PUT \
  -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" \
  -F "required_status_checks[strict]=false" \
  -F "required_status_checks[contexts][]=Cloud golden-path browser E2E" \
  -F "enforce_admins=false" \
  -F "required_pull_request_reviews=null" \
  -F "restrictions=null"

# clawmetry-landing: add one required check
gh api repos/vivekchand/clawmetry-landing/branches/main/protection \
  --method PUT \
  -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" \
  -F "required_status_checks[strict]=false" \
  -F "required_status_checks[contexts][]=Landing golden path (C3)" \
  -F "enforce_admins=false" \
  -F "required_pull_request_reviews=null" \
  -F "restrictions=null"
```

Once these are set, the next merge attempt on any PR with a failing E2E will be blocked. C6 flips to GREEN immediately.

**After C6 is done: the 7-consecutive-day countdown begins.** The cron will post a final summary and request disabling the trigger after 7 clean days.

---

## Fire log

| Fire | Timestamp | Gap closed | PR | Criterion |
|------|-----------|------------|----|-----------|
| 1 | 2026-05-26T00:00Z | C5 visual-diff gateway-token -- added explicit auth probe in e2e-critical, made health check fail with exit 1, added curl /api/auth/check annotation before Playwright. | #2147 | C5 |
| 2 | 2026-05-27T00:00Z | C3 landing golden path -- entire test suite absent from clawmetry-landing. Added run_landing.py + test_landing_golden_path.py + landing-golden-path.yml. | clawmetry-landing#325 | C3 |
| 3 | 2026-05-28T00:00Z | C4 daemon pair + event flow -- test_step_3 and test_step_4 were @pytest.mark.skip stubs. Replaced with DaemonSim-backed tests. | clawmetry-cloud#1168 (merged) | C4 |
| 4 | 2026-05-31T00:00Z | Status audit: confirmed C1/C2/C3/C4/C5/C7 all GREEN from live PR check runs. C6 is the only remaining RED criterion. Documented exact required-status-check job names and gh CLI commands above. No code change needed -- C6 is a one-time manual admin action. | (tracking issue update) | C6 blocked on manual |

---

## Stop condition

All 7 criteria green for 7 consecutive days triggers a final summary here and disables the cron trigger at https://claude.ai/code/scheduled.

For anyone who comes across this post, I wanted to share part of my AI journey.

I primarily run local models on consumer hardware (RX 9070 XT 16GB + 3060ti 8GB) and spend a lot of time testing coding agents and models.

I eventually settled on Little-Coder because it is:

* Has strong anti-loop protection (my favorite feature, which I jokingly call "Loopinus Maximus")

Many coding agents get stuck in loops and require constant babysitting. Little-Coder has been much more resilient in that regard.

If you have any model reccomendation please post, all of us are always looking for the holy grail.

**Important:** These are not scientific benchmarks. I turned the process into a blind tournament and used ChatGPT to generate prompts, evaluate submissions, and keep scoring consistent.

🥈 Qwen3.6-28B-A3B-REAP20-Q4_K_M

### Benchmark 1 – Deluxe Snake

Built a premium arcade-quality Snake game with progression, effects, achievements, menus, save systems, and multiple game modes.

**Tested:** Creativity, product thinking, game architecture, and gameplay quality.

Winner: 🥇 REAM-192

### Benchmark 2 – Personal Task Manager

**Tested:** Software engineering fundamentals, architecture, validation, and reliability.

Winner: 🥇 REAM-192

### Benchmark 3 – Mini Version Control System

Winner: 🥇 REAM-192

### Benchmark 4 – Log Analyzer

### Benchmark 5 – Loopinus Maximus

The trap benchmark.

Models had to:

* Build an application
* List assumptions
* Challenge those assumptions
* Find failures
* Diagnose failures
* Repair failures
* Explain remaining uncertainty

The goal was not to prove correctness.

The goal was to determine how well the model could discover when it was wrong.

**Tested:** Root-cause analysis, falsification, debugging discipline, and intellectual honesty.

Winner: 🥇 REAM-192 (photo finish)

---

# Final Assessment

### 🥇 REAM-192

The strongest overall engineering model.

Strengths:

* Strong architecture
* Excellent debugging discipline
* Consistent across all benchmarks

---

### 🥈 REAP20

The most balanced challenger.

Strengths:

### 🥉 Genesis

The biggest surprise.

Strengths:

* Strong falsification mindset
* Consistently overperformed expectations

---

### 4️⃣ Ornith

Most improved model.

Strengths:

* Creative solutions
* Strong reasoning
* Improved significantly throughout the tournament

---

# My Recommendations

If I could keep only three coding models installed today:

1. 🥇 REAM-192

3. 🥉 Genesis

After five engineering benchmarks, REAM-192 remained the most complete coding model I tested.

source_title: Allow switching execution context to Dedicated Workers
source_content:
Hi there,

First off, thank you for the `mcp-server` project. It's a fantastic tool and a great starting point for programmatic browser interaction.

We are integrating `mcp-server` into the [Neo.mjs framework](https://github.com/neomjs/neo) workflow to give our AI development agent, Gemini 2.5 Pro, the ability to 'see' and interact with the UI. While working on this integration, the agent itself identified this limitation and helped draft this feature request.

Our framework is built on an "Off the Main Thread" (OMT) architecture, where nearly all application logic runs inside workers. This creates a challenge for debugging that we believe `mcp-server` is uniquely positioned to solve.

**The Problem:**
The standard Chrome DevTools UI provides a dropdown that allows developers to switch the console's execution context between the main thread and any active workers. This is essential for debugging, as it allows for direct interaction with the global scope of each thread.

Currently, the `mcp-server` appears to be bound to the main thread's execution context. While some error messages from dedicated workers might bubble up, it's impossible to interact with the worker's scope. For example, we can't run a command like `Neo.get('my-component-id')` to inspect a live object that exists only within the worker.

**Proposed Feature:**
Could a mechanism be introduced to replicate the context-switching functionality of the real DevTools?

Ideally, this would involve:
1.  An API to list all available execution contexts (e.g., main thread, dedicated worker 1, dedicated worker 2).
2.  An API to set the active execution context for the `mcp-server` connection.

Once the context is switched to a specific worker, all subsequent `Runtime.evaluate` calls would execute within that worker's global scope. This would provide the powerful, interactive debugging experience needed for modern, multi-threaded web applications.

We believe this feature would unlock a new level of debugging and automation for any project that leverages dedicated workers.

We'd be happy to provide more details on our use case or assist in testing. Thanks for considering this!

source_title: gh shim recursively selects another aidevops shim after hot deploy
source_content:
## Description

The aidevops `gh` shim can recursively select a different aidevops `gh` shim as its downstream executable when a long-running session has an immutable runtime-bundle shim and the mutable installed shim both ahead of native GitHub CLI on `PATH`.

Each shim excludes only its own directory in `_find_real_gh()`. The runtime-bundle shim therefore selects the installed shim, while the installed shim selects the runtime-bundle shim. Even `gh --version` then alternates between the two wrappers until an external timeout kills the chain. GitHub is never contacted.

This is the `gh` equivalent of the cross-generation Git-shim defect fixed by #27405 / PR #27410, but that fix changed only the Git shim and canonical Git policy. It did not harden `.agents/scripts/gh`.

The failure blocks issue reads, claims, PR operations, diagnostics, pulse routines, and any framework helper that invokes ordinary `gh`. It initially resembles GitHub rate limiting, but direct API and native-CLI checks show healthy connectivity and ample quota.

## Expected Behavior

The shim must resolve one trusted native GitHub CLI executable and invoke it after at most one aidevops shim. Hot deployment must remain safe for long-running sessions pinned to an older immutable runtime bundle.

The documented `AIDEVOPS_GH_SHIM_DISABLE=1` bypass must always reach native `gh`, even when multiple aidevops shim generations are present on `PATH`.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```bash
/usr/bin/time -f 'elapsed=%e exit=%x' timeout 3s env \
  PATH=<runtime-bundle>/agents/scripts:<installed-aidevops>/agents/scripts:/usr/bin:/bin \
  gh --version
```

**Actual output**:

```text
Command exited with non-zero status 124
elapsed=3.00 exit=124
```

The same timeout occurs with the documented bypass:

```bash
timeout 3s env AIDEVOPS_GH_SHIM_DISABLE=1 \
  PATH=<runtime-bundle>/agents/scripts:<installed-aidevops>/agents/scripts:/usr/bin:/bin \
  gh --version
```

Control cases isolate the two-wrapper interaction:

```text
runtime-bundle shim + native gh: exit 0 in 0.08s
installed shim + native gh:      exit 0 in 0.08s
both shims + native gh:          exit 124 after 3.00s
/usr/bin/gh api rate_limit:      4,958/5,000 REST requests remaining
direct api.github.com request:   HTTP 200 in approximately 0.15s
```

**Blocked child command**:

```text
<other-aidevops-shim>/agents/scripts/gh --version
```

Resolution alternates by generation:

```text
runtime-bundle gh
  -> installed gh
    -> runtime-bundle gh
      -> installed gh
        -> repeats until timeout
```

**Backend state**:

GitHub is not the blocker. DNS and direct HTTPS connectivity were healthy, native `/usr/bin/gh` returned immediately, and the authenticated REST pool had 4,958 of 5,000 requests remaining.

**Expected output**:

```text
gh version 2.96.0 (2026-07-02)
```

The command should complete promptly and execute native GitHub CLI exactly once.

**Causal code**:

- `.agents/scripts/gh:165-181`: `_find_real_gh()` excludes only `_SHIM_DIR`, then accepts the first other executable named `gh` on `PATH`. It does not reject other runtime-bundle, mutable installed, repository, or aidevops bin shims by resolved identity.
- `.agents/scripts/gh:381-388`: ordinary passthrough commands resolve and `exec` the incorrectly selected wrapper before the later recursion guard is reached.
- `.agents/scripts/gh:395-400`: the emergency bypass uses the same defective resolver, so it also recurses.
- `.agents/scripts/gh:407-409`: the recursion guard again calls `_find_real_gh()`; with two generations it forwards to the other shim instead of native `gh`.

The deployed `gh` shim was byte-identical across aidevops v3.32.61, v3.32.70, v3.32.87, and the mutable installed copy. The defect is therefore latent rather than introduced by PR #27410. Immutable runtime bundles and hot deployment activate the invalid assumption that “not this shim” means “native GitHub CLI,” matching the architectural failure identified in #27405.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a long-running session whose `PATH` begins with an immutable runtime-bundle `agents/scripts` directory.
2. Keep the mutable installed `agents/scripts` directory later on `PATH`, before native GitHub CLI.
3. Confirm both locations contain the aidevops `gh` shim.
4. Run `gh --version`, `gh auth status`, or any GitHub operation.
5. Observe timeout with both shims, while either shim alone reaches native `gh` immediately.
6. Repeat with `AIDEVOPS_GH_SHIM_DISABLE=1`; observe that the documented bypass also times out.

## Workarounds Applied

- Invoked `/usr/bin/gh` directly for bounded read-only diagnosis and GitHub API checks.
- Used a sanitized `PATH` containing only one aidevops `gh` shim plus system binaries when shim behavior was required.
- Added external `timeout` bounds to prevent recursive calls from hanging the session indefinitely.
- Avoided attributing the symptom to rate limiting until direct quota and transport checks disproved it.

These are containment measures. Framework helpers and long-running automation still call ordinary `gh` and remain vulnerable.

## Recommended Fix Considerations

1. Reuse the trusted-native-executable strategy and cross-generation identity rejection developed for #27405, adapted for GitHub CLI.
2. Reject every aidevops-managed `gh` candidate by canonical/resolved identity, including immutable runtime bundles, mutable installed paths, repository shims, and aidevops bin paths.
3. Add an immediate recursion sentinel that fails closed with a bounded diagnostic rather than invoking another candidate wrapper.
4. Ensure the emergency bypass resolves native `gh` without entering instrumentation, signature, privacy, or normal resolver paths that can recurse.
5. Preserve portability: do not assume `/usr/bin/gh` is the only valid native location. Homebrew and other supported installations need a trusted resolution path.
6. Treat instrumentation as fail-open, but do not let fail-open behavior select another policy shim.
7. Consider a shared native-tool resolver for `git`, `gh`, and future PATH shims so this defect class cannot recur independently in each wrapper.
8. Keep hot-deployed immutable sessions supported; requiring users to restart every session would reduce exposure but would not correct executable identity.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test places two distinct aidevops `gh` shim generations before native `gh` on `PATH`; either entry shim invokes native `gh` exactly once without recursion.
- A test covers runtime-bundle, mutable installed, repository, bin, and symlinked shim candidates.
- `AIDEVOPS_GH_SHIM_DISABLE=1` reaches native `gh` with multiple generations present.
- Recursive re-entry exits immediately with a bounded, actionable diagnostic.
- Ordinary passthrough commands such as `gh --version` and intercepted commands such as `gh issue view` are both covered.
- Existing signature injection, privacy scanning, headless write protection, read rewriting, and API instrumentation tests continue to pass.
- Linux and macOS/Homebrew native-resolution fixtures are covered.
- A bounded concurrent test confirms stable process depth and count after hot-deployment-style PATH composition.

## Environment

- aidevops v3.32.87 (latest observed during diagnostics: v3.32.88)
- OpenCode interactive session with immutable runtime-bundle paths
- Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- bash 5.2.21
- GitHub CLI 2.96.0

## Additional Context

This is not Linux-specific in mechanism. Linux supplied the reproducer, but the resolver and recursion behavior are Bash/PATH-based. Any supported platform can trigger it when two aidevops shim identities precede native `gh`.

Related: #27405 established the same invariant for Git: “not this shim” is not sufficient proof that a candidate is native. PR #27410 fixed that specific Git path and was released in v3.32.70. This report requests the equivalent correction for `gh`, with consideration for consolidating native executable resolution so future shims inherit the invariant.

<!-- aidevops:sig -->

source_title: status: bound remote version probes and report per-component timeout diagnostics
source_content:
## Problem

On `homeboy 0.283.0+dff088da7059`, `homeboy status wp-build-runtime --timings` completes `resolve_project_components` (473ms) and `read_local_versions` (5ms), then stalls indefinitely at `fetch_remote_versions`. The command exceeds 120 seconds without rendering a dashboard or identifying the specific component probe.

This is related to #7378 but has a narrower, reproducible blocking phase: remote version collection.

## Expected behavior

- `--timings` reports phase progress and the dashboard returns within a bounded interval.
- Network, git, SSH, release, and component probes have independent deadlines.
- A failed or timed-out component remains visible with an explicit actionable diagnostic; it is not silently omitted.
- Timed-out child process groups are cleaned up.

## Reproduction

1. Run `homeboy status wp-build-runtime --timings`.
2. Observe `fetch_remote_versions...` as the last phase line.
3. The command exceeds two minutes without status output.

## AI assistance
- **AI assistance:** Yes
- **Tool(s):** OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol via OpenCode direct general coding subagent
- **Used for:** Reproducing the stalled status phase and drafting the focused regression report.

source_title: Show free-shipping progress right after add-to-cart (highest-leverage moment)
source_content:
## Problem
Issue #218 added precise free-shipping progress to the cart view, but the single most effective moment to nudge 'add $X more for free shipping' is the instant a shopper adds an item, the classic post-add upsell. The add_to_cart response does not carry that, so the assistant misses the best chance to lift order value.

## Change
Include the same grounded free_shipping progress (threshold, remaining, qualified) in the add_to_cart tool response when a free-shipping threshold is configured, computed from the real cart total via the existing Fahad_AI_Tools::free_shipping_progress() helper.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] add_to_cart success response includes a free_shipping field only when a threshold is configured; absent otherwise.
- [ ] The remaining amount is computed from the real cart total (floored at 0) and matches the shared helper.
- [ ] Existing add_to_cart behaviour (success, urls, variations, failure paths) is unchanged.
- [ ] TDD, 100% coverage on includes/ maintained, zero em/en dashes.
- [ ] Released to GitHub + WordPress.org SVN + woo demo store.

source_title: SYSTEM_PROMPT instructs the LLM to call 'query_multimodal_ai' but the registered tool is 'query_multimodal_api'
source_content:
**Severity:** Low · **Area:** Lens: contracts · **Category:** `contract-drift`
**Location:** `services/agent/selene_agent/utils/config.py:198`

### What's wrong
The agent system prompt says camera snapshot URLs 'will often need to be sent for analysis using "query_multimodal_ai"', but mcp_general_tools/mcp_server.py registers the tool as name="query_multimodal_api" (line 98; the Python method is query_multimodal_ai, the exposed MCP name is _api). The prompt names a tool that does not exist in the tool list handed to the model.

The model follows the prompt literally and emits a tool call named query_multimodal_ai after a camera-snapshot tool; the call fails with 'unknown tool', costing an extra correction iteration per turn (or a failed vision analysis on models that don't retry), particularly on smaller local models that trust prompt text over the tool schema list.

Change the prompt text to query_multimodal_api (or rename the registered tool to match).

source_title: What is the optimal algorithm for the game 2048?
source_content:
I developed a 2048 AI using expectimax optimization, instead of the minimax search used by @ovolve's algorithm. The AI simply performs maximization over all possible moves, followed by expectation over all possible tile spawns (weighted by the probability of the tiles, i.e. 10% for a 4 and 90% for a 2). As far as I'm aware, it is not possible to prune expectimax optimization (except to remove branches that are exceedingly unlikely), and so the algorithm used is a carefully optimized brute force search.

Performance

The AI in its default configuration (max search depth of 8) takes anywhere from 10ms to 200ms to execute a move, depending on the complexity of the board position. In testing, the AI achieves an average move rate of 5-10 moves per second over the course of an entire game. If the search depth is limited to 6 moves, the AI can easily execute 20+ moves per second, which makes for some interesting watching.

To assess the score performance of the AI, I ran the AI 100 times (connected to the browser game via remote control). For each tile, here are the proportions of games in which that tile was achieved at least once:



The minimum score over all runs was 124024; the maximum score achieved was 794076. The median score is 387222. The AI never failed to obtain the 2048 tile (so it never lost the game even once in 100 games); in fact, it achieved the 8192 tile at least once in every run!

Here's the screenshot of the best run:



This game took 27830 moves over 96 minutes, or an average of 4.8 moves per second. 

Implementation

My approach encodes the entire board (16 entries) as a single 64-bit integer (where tiles are the nybbles, i.e. 4-bit chunks). On a 64-bit machine, this enables the entire board to be passed around in a single machine register.

Bit shift operations are used to extract individual rows and columns. A single row or column is a 16-bit quantity, so a table of size 65536 can encode transformations which operate on a single row or column. For example, moves are implemented as 4 lookups into a precomputed "move effect table" which describes how each move affects a single row or column (for example, the "move right" table contains the entry "1122 -> 0023" describing how the row [2,2,4,4] becomes the row [0,0,4,8] when moved to the right).

Scoring is also done using table lookup. The tables contain heuristic scores computed on all possible rows/columns, and the resultant score for a board is simply the sum of the table values across each row and column.

This board representation, along with the table lookup approach for movement and scoring, allows the AI to search a huge number of game states in a short period of time (over 10,000,000 game states per second on one core of my mid-2011 laptop).

The expectimax search itself is coded as a recursive search which alternates between "expectation" steps (testing all possible tile spawn locations and values, and weighting their optimized scores by the probability of each possibility), and "maximization" steps (testing all possible moves and selecting the one with the best score). The tree search terminates when it sees a previously-seen position (using a transposition table), when it reaches a predefined depth limit, or when it reaches a board state that is highly unlikely (e.g. it was reached by getting 6 "4" tiles in a row from the starting position). The typical search depth is 4-8 moves.

Heuristics

Several heuristics are used to direct the optimization algorithm towards favorable positions. The precise choice of heuristic has a huge effect on the performance of the algorithm. The various heuristics are weighted and combined into a positional score, which determines how "good" a given board position is. The optimization search will then aim to maximize the average score of all possible board positions. The actual score, as shown by the game, is not used to calculate the board score, since it is too heavily weighted in favor of merging tiles (when delayed merging could produce a large benefit).

Initially, I used two very simple heuristics, granting "bonuses" for open squares and for having large values on the edge. These heuristics performed pretty well, frequently achieving 16384 but never getting to 32768.

Petr Morávek (@xificurk) took my AI and added two new heuristics. The first heuristic was a penalty for having non-monotonic rows and columns which increased as the ranks increased, ensuring that  non-monotonic rows of small numbers would not strongly affect the score, but non-monotonic rows of large numbers hurt the score substantially. The second heuristic counted the number of potential merges (adjacent equal values) in addition to open spaces. These two heuristics served to push the algorithm towards monotonic boards (which are easier to merge), and towards board positions with lots of merges (encouraging it to align merges where possible for greater effect).

Furthermore, Petr also optimized the heuristic weights using a "meta-optimization" strategy (using an algorithm called CMA-ES), where the weights themselves were adjusted to obtain the highest possible average score.

The effect of these changes are extremely significant. The algorithm went from achieving the 16384 tile around 13% of the time to achieving it over 90% of the time, and the algorithm began to achieve 32768 over 1/3 of the time (whereas the old heuristics never once produced a 32768 tile).

I believe there's still room for improvement on the heuristics. This algorithm definitely isn't yet "optimal", but I feel like it's getting pretty close.



That the AI achieves the 32768 tile in over a third of its games is a huge milestone; I will be surprised to hear if any human players have achieved 32768 on the official game (i.e. without using tools like savestates or undo). I think the 65536 tile is within reach!

You can try the AI for yourself. The code is available at https://github.com/nneonneo/2048-ai.
